quests.hint: Each sentence makes a different point about how complex the same debate really is.

quests.title: Summary Synapse
quests.coreRule: Topic sentences establish the framework; anchor definitions to their functional purpose rather than incidental words.
quests.paragraphTopic: Precise paraphrasing of a policy's claimed effect
quests.instruction: Match each version with its precise meaning.

detailedPairs.key: [L140-Q3-0] This policy will fix the problem.
detailedPairs.cleanKey: This policy will fix the problem.
detailedPairs.value: This claims the policy will completely solve the issue, with full confidence.
detailedPairs.rationale: Connects "This policy will fix the problem." directly to the defining quality "claims, policy, completely".

detailedPairs.key: [L140-Q3-1] This policy might help with part of the problem.
detailedPairs.cleanKey: This policy might help with part of the problem.
detailedPairs.value: This claims the policy could offer partial improvement, with real uncertainty about how much.
detailedPairs.rationale: Connects "This policy might help with part of the problem." directly to the defining quality "claims, policy, could".

detailedPairs.key: [L140-Q3-2] This policy has, in some cases, made the problem worse.
detailedPairs.cleanKey: This policy has, in some cases, made the problem worse.
detailedPairs.value: This claims the policy has actually had a harmful effect in certain specific situations.
detailedPairs.rationale: Connects "This policy has, in some cases, made the problem worse." directly to the defining quality "claims, policy, actually".

detailedPairs.key: [L140-Q3-3] This policy is unlikely to make any real difference.
detailedPairs.cleanKey: This policy is unlikely to make any real difference.
detailedPairs.value: This claims the policy probably won't have a meaningful effect either way.
detailedPairs.rationale: Connects "This policy is unlikely to make any real difference." directly to the defining quality "claims, policy, probably".

quests.explanation: The first claims total success, will fix. The second claims only partial, uncertain help, might help with part. The third claims a specific, negative effect in certain cases, has made worse. The fourth is different from all three — it claims the policy probably won't matter either way.
quests.hint: These four sentences look almost identical but differ in a small but important way — how confidently and how completely each one claims the policy works.
